question: Explain when borrowing costs may be capitalised under AS 16 'Borrowing Costs'. When should capitalisation commence, be suspended and cease?
sources: AS 16 Borrowing Costs - definitions, recognition, commencement, suspension and cessation of capitalisation

points.label: Qualifying asset
points.description: An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale; ordinarily twelve months is treated as substantial unless a shorter period is justified.
points.basis: AS 16, definition of qualifying asset and its explanation

points.label: What is capitalised
points.description: Borrowing costs directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of a qualifying asset are capitalised as part of its cost; other borrowing costs are expensed in the period incurred.

points.label: Specific and general borrowings
points.description: For funds borrowed specifically, the amount is the actual cost less income from temporary investment of those funds; for general borrowings, a capitalisation rate (weighted average cost) is applied to the expenditure on the asset.
points.basis: AS 16, borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation

points.label: Commencement
points.description: Capitalisation starts when expenditure on the asset is being incurred, borrowing costs are being incurred, and activities needed to prepare the asset are in progress.

points.label: Suspension
points.description: Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted (not for temporary delays that are a necessary part of the process).

points.label: Cessation
points.description: Capitalisation stops when substantially all activities needed to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale are complete; for an asset completed in parts, for each part usable on its own when that part is complete.
